notes: Historical EBIT is taken as Otis' total company operating profit from the segment financial data note (GAAP operating profit basis). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1781335/000178133525000010/otis-20241231.htm))

Working capital (NWC) is computed as total current assets minus total current liabilities, but Otis shows a working-capital deficit in each historical year; per 'absolute values' instruction, the JSON uses the magnitude (positive) for NWC and NWC_pct_sales. This is a sign-convention approximation—ensure your DCF engine applies the intended deficit sign consistently. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1781335/000178133525000010/otis-20241231.htm))

Tax rate (tax_rate) is set to a normalized GAAP-effective proxy using FY2025 GAAP figures (tax expense / pre-tax income) rather than the unusually low FY2024 effective tax rate driven by litigation-related tax impacts. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

WACC is a placeholder from a market-data summary (StockAnalysis) and should be replaced with a fully derived cost of capital in your model governance process if required. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/otis/statistics/))

Peer comps: NTM EV/Revenue and NTM EV/EBITDA and P/E NTM were not confirmable from accessible NTM sources for most peers within this run; those fields are left null except for thyssenkrupp where free valuation ratios were available as imperfect proxies. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/quote/otc/TYEKF/statistics/?utm_source=openai))
Current price uses the latest available close from market data tooling (last trade time on Mar 20, 2026); since Mar 21, 2026 is a weekend, this is treated as the effective 'as-of' market price.

Assumption gaps: 'investments' and 'nol_utilization_pct' are set to null because a directly usable annual investments and NOL utilization rate were not captured explicitly in accessible disclosures in this run.

catalysts: Follow-through on FY2026 outlook (organic sales up low-to-mid single digits; adjusted EPS up mid-to-high single digits). ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

Sustained modernization order momentum improving backlog quality and service attachment rates. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

Further service margin expansion from productivity initiatives and pricing actions. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))
company_overview: Leading elevator and escalator manufacturing, installation, and service provider with a large installed base and recurring service revenue. ([otis.com](https://www.otis.com/en/us?utm_source=openai))

Two operating segments: New Equipment (manufacture/install) and Service (maintenance, repair, and modernization). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1781335/000178133525000010/otis-20241231.htm))
Serves ~2.5M customer units worldwide and moves ~2.5B people per day through its products and service network. ([otis.com](https://www.otis.com/en/us?utm_source=openai))
current_context: FY2025 net sales were $14.431B (flat organic growth); GAAP operating profit was $2.133B with operating profit margin of 14.8%. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

Management guided FY2026 organic sales growth up low-to-mid single digits and adjusted EPS up mid-to-high single digits; adjusted free cash flow expected at $1.6B–$1.7B. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

Capital return remained active: Otis reported repurchases of approximately $800M in FY2025 alongside continued dividend growth. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Service flywheel supports resilience: FY2025 service growth and margin expansion underpin the base-case path to gradually higher EBIT margin. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

Modernization demand provides a durable earnings engine; management reported continued strength in modernization backlog momentum entering 2026. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

UpLift and cost-structure improvements are assumed to translate into modest, sustained margin expansion rather than step-function changes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1781335/000178133525000010/otis-20241231.htm))

Base-case capital intensity is kept conservative using historical capex-to-sales and D&A-to-sales ratios from GAAP cash flow disclosures. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1781335/000178133525000010/otis-20241231.htm))

Working capital is modeled with normalization versus the large 2025 deficit, reflecting post-separation balance-sheet dynamics and a return toward historical norms. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))
key_risks: Demand volatility in new equipment and modernization (macro and regional construction cycles). ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

Margin pressure from inflation, labor costs, and foreign exchange translating into higher operating expenses. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))

Working-capital normalization may take longer than modeled, reducing free cash flow conversion. ([otisinvestors.com](https://www.otisinvestors.com/news/news-details/2026/OTIS-REPORTS-FOURTH-QUARTER-AND-FULL-YEAR-2025-RESULTS/default.aspx))
Execution risk around UpLift transformation and cost-structure delivery. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1781335/000178133525000010/otis-20241231.htm))
